metadata.validation_case_name: Solid-State Battery Filament Formation - In-Situ Tomography
metadata.purpose: Validate HIGH-FIDELITY System E modeling with full temporal and positional complexity

reference_paper.title: Filament-Induced Failure in Lithium-Reservoir-Free Solid-State Batteries
reference_paper.technique: In-situ 3D X-ray computed tomography (XCT) during battery cycling
reference_paper.key_result: X-ray tomography reveals filament growth faster at high local current density regions

metadata.beamline: HEX (27-ID) - High Energy Engineering X-ray Scattering
metadata.validation_approach: HIGH-FIDELITY System E - Explicitly model temporal and positional acquisition complexity
metadata.system_e_focus: This case demonstrates full System E complexity: tomographic sample rotation (positional) + time-resolved in-situ cycling (temporal)

validation_strategy.description: We will treat the solid-state battery as having PARTIALLY_KNOWN properties (solid electrolyte structure and electrochemistry known, filament formation dynamics and fracture mechanisms UNKNOWN), then use gap closure to infer failure mechanisms from 3D tomography data collected during in-situ cycling.
known_beforehand: Solid electrolyte material: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) or similar
Cell architecture: Lithium-reservoir-free (no excess Li anode)
Applied stack pressure: Variable (low vs high pressure conditions)
Electrochemical parameters: Current density, voltage, capacity
Nominal electrolyte structure: Crystal lattice, grain boundaries
Expected failure mode: Lithium filament penetration and/or solid electrolyte fracture
discovered_by_experiment: Filament growth rate as function of local current density
Crack formation and propagation in solid electrolyte
Spatial distribution of lithium plating irregularities
Time evolution of filament penetration through electrolyte
validation_strategy.gap_closure_target: Can we infer filament formation mechanisms and pressure-dependent failure pathways from 3D tomography time series?
validation_strategy.success_criteria: Gap closure should propose: (1) Filament growth correlates with local current density, (2) Low pressure → irregular plating, (3) High pressure → uniform plating but stress-induced fracture, (4) Time-dependent filament penetration

experimental_components.notes: HIGH ENERGY IS CRITICAL - Must penetrate through battery cell (several mm thick including steel casing). Lower energy (e.g., soft X-rays) would be absorbed.

experimental_components.description: Monochromator and focusing optics optimized for high-energy X-rays (30-100 keV)

physical_properties.typical_mode: Monochromatic at 60-70 keV for battery imaging
physical_properties.beam_size_at_sample: 4 mm field of view (matched to battery electrode area)
physical_properties.coherence: Partial coherence (not critical for absorption imaging)

experimental_functions: Select X-ray energy (60-70 keV for solid-state battery)
Condition beam for uniform illumination across sample

experimental_components.component_name: Custom In-Situ Battery Cell for Tomography
experimental_components.description: Custom electrochemical cell designed for X-ray transparency and in-situ tomography during cycling

physical_properties.stack_pressure: Controlled (low vs high pressure conditions tested)

experimental_components.description: Lithium-reservoir-free solid-state battery with UNKNOWN filament formation dynamics and fracture mechanisms

experimental_components.gap_closure_goal: Infer filament formation mechanisms and pressure-dependent failure pathways from 3D tomography time series collected during in-situ battery cycling

constraints.spatial_resolution: 1.3 μm voxel size (must resolve filaments and cracks)
constraints.temporal_resolution: ~minutes to hours (tomography scan time limits time resolution)
constraints.sample_stability: Battery must remain stable during ~10-30 minute tomography scan
constraints.electrochemical_constraints: Cycling must continue during tomography (operando mode)

experimental_functions: Scatter X-rays to produce radiographic projections (absorption contrast)
Evolve filament structure under electrochemical cycling
Generate time-dependent 3D morphology encoding failure mechanisms
experimental_components.notes: THIS IS SYSTEM D - THE KNOWLEDGE GAP. Filament formation dynamics (growth rate, 3D morphology, failure pathway) are UNKNOWN and will be inferred from tomography.

experimental_components.component_name: Fast Area Detector with Tomographic Sample Rotation Stage
experimental_components.description: High-energy X-ray area detector with automated sample rotation for computed tomography

detector_hardware.detector_type: Perkin Elmer 1621 or Varex 4343 (scintillator-based, high energy)

acquisition_strategy._comment: THIS IS THE KEY HIGH-FIDELITY SECTION - Full temporal and positional complexity
acquisition_strategy.measurement_type: 3D X-ray computed tomography (XCT) with in-situ cycling

temporal_strategy.flat_field_frames: 10 frames (before scan, beam profile without sample)
temporal_strategy.adaptive_strategies: May increase scan frequency near failure (when voltage drops)

positional_strategy.detector_distance: Fixed (~50-200 mm for 4 mm FOV with 1.3 μm resolution)
positional_strategy.magnification: Optical magnification via scintillator + lens system

multi_modal_capability.diffraction_mode: Optional (can switch to diffraction detector for phase ID)

experimental_functions: Acquire radiographic projections at each rotation angle
Rotate sample through 180° (1000-1500 angles) for tomographic reconstruction
Repeat tomography scans during battery cycling (time-resolved 3D imaging)
Capture electrochemical data synchronized with tomography timestamps

measured_observables.primary_observable: Time series of 3D tomographic volumes showing filament evolution
measured_observables.tomographic_scan: 1000-1500 projections → 3D volume (4 mm)^3 with 1.3 μm resolution
measured_observables.spatial_resolution: 1.3 μm (can resolve lithium filaments and cracks)
measured_observables.contrast_mechanism: Absorption (lithium metal appears dark, LLZO appears gray)

experimental_components.notes: HIGH-FIDELITY SYSTEM E - This component explicitly models BOTH temporal (time-resolved tomography during cycling) and positional (sample rotation through 1000+ angles) complexity. Total measurement space: (x, y, z, time, angle) = 4D reconstructed + rotation dimension during acquisition.
blop_optimization_opportunities: Adaptive integration time: Shorter exposures when sample is stable, longer near features
Smart angular sampling: Dense sampling near features of interest (filaments), sparse elsewhere
Adaptive scan frequency: Increase tomography rate when battery voltage indicates imminent failure
Multi-objective optimization: Minimize radiation dose while maintaining resolution and temporal sampling
Trajectory optimization: Non-uniform angular sampling (golden ratio, Fibonacci) for faster scans
Region-of-interest tomography: Image only active region (lithium plating zone) for faster acquisition

experimental_components.description: Computational pipeline to reconstruct 3D volumes from projection data and analyze filament morphology

physical_properties.reconstruction_algorithm: Filtered back-projection (FBP) or iterative reconstruction (SIRT, TV)
physical_properties.computational_cost: High - reconstruct 3×10^9 voxels per scan × 20 scans
physical_properties.input_data: 1000-1500 projections (2048×2048 pixels each) per tomography scan
physical_properties.output_data: 3D volume (4 mm)^3 with 1.3 μm voxels, 8-bit or 16-bit grayscale
physical_properties.data_reduction: Minimal - tomography data is already spatially integrated
physical_properties.segmentation: Thresholding or machine learning to identify lithium filaments and cracks
physical_properties.quantification: Filament volume, surface area, growth rate, crack length
physical_properties.real_time_processing: Fast reconstruction (<5 min per scan) enables in-situ feedback
physical_properties.4D_analysis: Track filament evolution over time (register 3D volumes from different scans)

experimental_functions: Reconstruct 3D volumes from tomographic projection data
Segment lithium filaments and cracks from solid electrolyte matrix
Quantify filament morphology (volume, tortuosity, growth direction)
Track time evolution (4D analysis: 3D + time)
Correlate filament growth with electrochemical data (current, voltage)
Identify failure mechanisms (filament penetration vs electrolyte fracture)

software_tools: Avizo or Dragonfly (3D rendering and quantification)
Custom Python scripts (4D tracking, filament growth analysis)

experimental_components.notes: THIS IS SYSTEM F - REQUIRED for tomography. Converts 2D projections → 3D volume → quantitative filament analysis. Without reconstruction, projection data is uninterpretable (can't resolve 3D structure).

physical_interactions.description: THIS IS THE CRITICAL DATA - Tomographic projections acquired during sample rotation. 3D reconstruction reveals filament morphology. Time series of 3D volumes reveals growth dynamics.
physical_interactions.system_e_complexity_note: This interaction involves BOTH positional (sample rotation through 1000+ angles) AND temporal (repeated scans over hours) complexity. Measurement space is 5D: (detector_x, detector_y, rotation_angle, scan_number, electrochemical_time).

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Radon transform inversion (FBP or iterative) converts projections to 3D volume
physical_interactions.description: System F performs tomographic reconstruction. 2D projections → 3D volume → filament segmentation → quantitative analysis. Without reconstruction, cannot infer 3D filament morphology or growth mechanisms.

notes.validation_approach: This HIGH-FIDELITY case demonstrates that System E is NOT just detector hardware, but includes acquisition strategy (temporal + positional). Gap closure must recognize that 3D filament morphology comes from tomographic reconstruction (System F), not direct measurement (System E projections).
notes.system_e_critical_complexity: System E involves sample rotation (1000+ angles) AND time-resolved measurement (repeated scans). Measurement space is 5D: (detector_x, detector_y, rotation_angle, scan_number, electrochemical_time).
notes.system_f_critical: System F is ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL for tomography. Without 3D reconstruction, 2D projections cannot reveal filament morphology. Reconstruction is THE OBSERVABLE (not projections).
notes.challenge: Tomography data is massive (80-400 GB per experiment). Fast reconstruction (GPU) enables in-situ feedback. Time resolution is limited by scan duration (~10-30 minutes per tomography).
notes.next_steps: This case establishes template for high-fidelity System E modeling. Future cases should include acquisition_strategy section with temporal + positional + BLOP opportunities.
